Jordan / Sean - see below for a concise competitive eval and proposed test plan. Attaching the detailed test plan and a comparison table.

Competitive summary (high level):
- Latency: Redwood typically shows lower p95 tail on long-context LLM workloads due to our continuous batching and KV cache management. Hyperscalers may have higher p99 due to per-request cold path and less aggressive batching by default.
- Cost: Hyperscalers often win on raw managed instance pricing for low-utilization workloads, but Redwoods batching and caching reduce cost-per-token at moderate-to-high throughput. We should present 2 cost scenarios (low, sustained).
- Regional availability / Residency: Hyperscalers have broad regions but customers often run into cross-region egress or higher tail latency; Redwood Private or Dedicated can be deployed to meet strict residency requirements.
- Operational experience: Our dev-first APIs + rollout tooling (canary, fallback) reduce risk during migration.

Proposed test plan (short):
1) Endpoints: deploy the same model variant in our hosted eu-west-1, us-east-1, us-west-2 endpoints. Provide endpoint URLs in the test plan.
2) Load: run 3 phases - baseline (10 RPS, 5 min), sustained (50 RPS, 10 min), stress (200 RPS, 5 min) while measuring p50/p95/p99 and error rates.
3) Cold vs Warm: run a cold-start batch after 30 minute idle, then measure warm steady-state latency.
4) Data residency: for the subset of accounts requiring EU-only residency, validate logs show eu-west-1 tenancy and no egress.
5) Outputs: p50/p95/p99 summaries, token counts, throughput, and a side-by-side cost estimate vs comparable hyperscaler configs.

Recommended acceptance criteria (quick):
- p95 <= 250ms for EU traffic in eu-west-1 (or at least demonstrably better than their current baseline)
- Error rate < 0.5% during sustained 50 RPS
- Clear plan for residency including audit log sample and KMS key zoning for Private if they request it

Attachments: multi_region_test_plan.md, redwood_vs_hyperscaler_table.csv

Happy to jump on the customer call once we have the baseline. I also included a short checklist for their network team (IPs, TLS certs, expected headers).

-Marissa
